scope: Extended demographic moderators on Big Five / HEXACO in Japanese samples (education, income/SES, marital status, occupation, region). Built on top of Kawamoto et al. 2015 sex x age prior (TIPI-J, N=4588).

papers.citation: Kawamoto, T. (2016). Cross-sectional age differences in the HEXACO personality: Results from a Japanese sample. Journal of Research in Personality, 62, 1-5. doi:10.1016/j.jrp.2016.03.001
papers.relevance: PRIMARY - uses education/income/marital status as covariates of HEXACO
papers.download_status: paywall_abstract_only (Elsevier/JRP). No preprint on ResearchGate/OSF located.
key_findings_qualitative: After controlling for education, annual income, marital status, gender: Emotionality NEGATIVELY associated with age
Extraversion, Agreeableness, Conscientiousness, Openness: NOT associated with age (after controls)

papers.citation: 川本哲也・小塩真司・阿部晋吾・坪田祐基・平島太郎・伊藤大幸・谷伊織 (2015). ビッグ・ファイブ・パーソナリティ特性の年齢差と性差：大規模横断調査による検討. 発達心理学研究, 26(2), 107-122.
papers.relevance: BASELINE prior (already in user hand) - confirmed open-access PDF
key_regression_findings: Agreeableness: linear age effect significant (positive) - older = more agreeable
Conscientiousness: linear age effect significant (positive) - older = more conscientious
Extraversion: only sex effect significant (B=0.466, SE=0.075, p<.001; female > male)
Openness: only sex effect significant (female lower than male)
Neuroticism: linear age effect + age x sex interaction significant; young women > young men, converges in older age

papers.citation: 吉野伸哉・小塩真司 (2021). 日本におけるBig Fiveパーソナリティの地域差の検討 ― 3つの大規模調査のデータセットを用いて ―. 環境心理学研究, 9(1), 19-33.

comparison_morans_I_usa_Rentfrow2013.note: USA shows much stronger spatial clustering than Japan; Japan effect sizes generally small

high: 首都圏 (東京・千葉・埼玉)

key_takeaways: Japan regional differences are SMALL in absolute terms (Moran's I << USA)
Only Extraversion shows significant nationwide spatial clustering
Metropolitan area (Tokyo/Kanagawa) higher Extraversion & Openness (matches selective migration hypothesis)
Tohoku district lower Conscientiousness, higher Neuroticism (harsh living environment hypothesis)
Okinawa: high Extraversion + Agreeableness, low Neuroticism (interpersonal warmth pattern)
Hokkaido: low Agreeableness across 3 datasets (consistent with Kitayama 2006 frontier hypothesis)

papers.citation: Lee, S.Y., & Ohtake, F. (2016). Is being agreeable a key to success or failure in the labor market? ISER Discussion Paper No. 960, Osaka University.
papers.relevance: PRIMARY for education attainment + income x personality in Japan (with US comparison)

sample.measure: TIPI 7-pt scale 1-7, single average per domain
sample.data_source: Osaka Univ COE Preference & Life Satisfaction Survey 2012

education_regression_japan_table2.note: DV = Years of Schooling (OLS), without parental education. Coefficient (SE). *p<.1 **p<.05 ***p<.01

papers.income_regression_japan_men_key: Agreeableness positive predictor of log(annual income) for Japanese men; agreeableness premium concentrated in large firms (≥1000 employees); contrast with US where agreeableness is income penalty for men.
key_takeaways: Agreeableness has the LARGEST and most significant effect on education in Japan (esp. male B=0.20)
Openness positive but weaker, small effect
Conscientiousness NOT significant for years of schooling in this Japanese sample (contrasts Western findings)
Agreeableness premium for income in Japanese men (esp. large firms) - opposite sign to US

Sex: males higher Assertiveness facet (d=0.42); females higher Aesthetic Sensitivity, Sociability (d=0.17)

papers.citation: Specht, J., Egloff, B., & Schmukle, S. C. (2011). Stability and change of personality across the life course: The impact of age and major life events on mean-level and rank-order stability of the Big Five. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 101, 862-882.
papers.relevance: _overseas reference for marital status effect on personality (Germany N=14,718)
key_qualitative: Personality predicts occurrence of major life events (selection effects)
Personality changes in response to events (socialization effects)
Marriage/divorce shown to relate to Big Five changes (small effects)
Conscientiousness shows monotonic rank-order stability increase across adulthood

papers.citation: Cobb-Clark, D. A., & Schurer, S. (2012). The stability of big-five personality traits. Economics Letters, 115(1), 11-15.
papers.relevance: _overseas - argues working-age personality is largely stable to income/employment shocks
key_qualitative: Mean population Big Five changes are SMALL and constant across age groups over 4 years
Intra-individual change largely unrelated to adverse life events
Important caveat for causal inference: demographic variables may PREDICT personality cross-sectionally but rarely CAUSE personality change in adulthood

education.evidence_strength: moderate (1 Japanese paper with explicit B, 1 abstract-only)

direction.Agreeableness: POSITIVE in Japan, especially men (B≈0.20 per TIPI-pt → years of schooling); CONTRAST with US where ns/negative
direction.Conscientiousness: NOT significant in Japan TIPI sample (B≈0.09 ns), unlike Western meta-analyses

education.caveat: Lee&Ohtake uses 2-item TIPI; reverse causality plausible (Cobb-Clark&Schurer)

direction.Agreeableness: POSITIVE for Japanese men, especially at large firms (≥1000 employees); opposite of US pattern
direction.Conscientiousness: Generally positive across countries (US data); Japan-specific Bs not extracted

marital_status.direction_overseas: Marriage selection: more agreeable/conscientious/extraverted more likely to marry; marriage socialization: small increase in conscientiousness/agreeableness, decrease in neuroticism (Specht 2011 Germany)
marital_status.japan_specific: Kawamoto 2016 controlled FOR marital status but did not publish marginal effects in accessible abstract. data: not_accessible

direction.by_occupation_overseas: Healthcare/teaching: high Agreeableness; Engineering/research: high Openness; Sales/management: high Extraversion; Office-admin: high Conscientiousness
direction.japan_distribution_men_lee_ohtake: 21% professional, 21% management/business, 18% construction, 16% service, 14% office-admin, 9% sales, 2% farming

region.magnitude: SMALL - prefecture mean z-scores typically |z| < 1.96; only Extraversion shows nationwide Moran's I significant (.27)
region.usage_note: Regional priors should be applied with weak weight given small absolute effect sizes
